questions.question: What is the general architectural pattern behind multimodal models?
options: Completely separate models are run independently with no shared components
Modality-specific encoders convert each input type (text, image, audio) into tokens/embeddings compatible with a shared transformer backbone that processes all of them together
Only text can ever be processed; images and audio are simply ignored
Multimodal models require a completely different attention mechanism for each modality
questions.explanation: Each modality has its own encoder converting it into a shared token/embedding representation, which then flows into the same underlying transformer architecture used for text, allowing the model to reason across modalities together.

questions.question: Why can adding image input support to a feature significantly increase cost, even though 'the model supports it'?
options: Image inputs are always free to process
Images are typically broken into many patches converted into tokens, often consuming far more tokens than an equivalent text description, directly increasing cost per request
Image processing has nothing to do with token-based pricing
This only applies to video, never to still images
questions.explanation: A single moderate-resolution image can consume hundreds to thousands of tokens, often substantially more than a short text description of the same content, making image support a real, calculable cost driver rather than a free capability unlock.

questions.question: A team wants to add image upload support to a chatbot 'since the model supports images now,' without further analysis. Which question best evaluates this proposal?
options: Should we just enable it since the capability exists?
Have we projected the token cost difference of image inputs at our expected scale, and do we have an evaluation approach specifically designed for this new modality?
Should we avoid ever using multimodal capabilities?
Is this feature technically impossible to build?
questions.explanation: Enabling a new modality has real cost implications (often much higher token consumption) and requires its own evaluation approach — neither should be assumed to come for free just because the underlying model technically supports it.
